Updated assessment using Beige Book context: The FOMC’s September 2018 statement is moderately hawkish and the Beige Book snippets reinforce that tone. Reports across districts (Dallas, Philadelphia, St. Louis, Kansas City) note continued job growth—particularly in construction—solid consumer spending in Dallas, and ongoing manufacturing activity in St. Louis. These district-level observations corroborate the Committee’s view of a strong economy and tight labor market, supporting its rate hike to 2–2.25% and guidance for further gradual increases. Coupled with SLOOS evidence of eased C&I lending standards and narrower spreads, the balance of information tilts a bit more hawkish than the initial read, with few offsets evident in the provided Beige Book references.
